dimensions.name: Intrinsic Motivation
dimensions.description: Measures the degree to which the individual is motivated by the inherent satisfaction of the work itself — curiosity, craft, autonomy, and flow — rather than external rewards or recognition.

dimensions.name: Extrinsic Motivation
dimensions.description: Measures the degree to which the individual is motivated by external rewards, recognition, status, visibility, and career progression.

dimensions.name: Values Alignment
dimensions.description: Measures the degree of alignment between the individual's personal values, sense of purpose, and the organisation's mission and ethics.

dimensions.name: Confidence & Self-Efficacy
dimensions.description: Measures the individual's belief in their own capability to succeed in their role — including confidence under pressure, ability to adapt, and conviction in their own skills.

dimensions.name: Growth Orientation
dimensions.description: Measures the degree to which the individual is motivated by growth, development, learning, and new challenges — versus mastery, stability, and doing what they already do well.

engagement_risk.name: Engagement Risk Sub-Score
engagement_risk.description: 6 supplemental items measuring engagement risk. Reported separately as Fueled / Flickering / Fading state; NOT included in core motivation composite.

archetypes.name: Achiever
archetypes.description: Extrinsic-dominant, Fueled. The Achiever is driven by recognition, progression, and visible results. They set ambitious targets, seek advancement, and thrive when their contributions are acknowledged and rewarded.
key_traits: Results-oriented and high-output
Strong drive for progression and visibility
High confidence in their capabilities

archetypes.name: Craftsman
archetypes.description: Intrinsic-dominant, Fueled. The Craftsman is deeply motivated by the quality and craft of the work itself. They find satisfaction in doing work well, in mastery of their discipline, and in alignment between their values and their work.
key_traits: Deep work satisfaction independent of external rewards
Commitment to quality and craftsmanship
Strong values alignment with their work

archetypes.name: Champion
archetypes.description: Relational-dominant, Fueled. The Champion is energised by developing others and building team capability. They thrive when they can see their impact through the growth and success of people around them.
key_traits: Strong people development orientation
High confidence that inspires others
Recognition from team success fuels sustained effort

archetypes.name: Explorer
archetypes.description: Intrinsic-dominant, Fueled. The Explorer is motivated by novelty, challenge, and new contexts. They thrive on steep learning curves, new environments, and the excitement of figuring things out.
key_traits: Thrives in new and challenging situations
Rapid learning capability
Comfortable with ambiguity and change

archetypes.name: Stalwart
archetypes.description: Purpose-driven, Fueled. The Stalwart is anchored in strong values alignment and intrinsic motivation, with lower growth orientation. They are loyal, steady, and deeply committed to the mission and purpose of the organisation.
key_traits: Deep institutional loyalty and commitment
Strong values alignment with the organisation
Reliable and consistent over long periods

archetypes.name: Restless
archetypes.description: Growth-driven, Flickering. The Restless has strong capability and high ambition but feels misaligned with the role's purpose or values. They are capable but not fully engaged.
key_traits: High capability and ambition
Strong growth orientation
Driven by progression and recognition

archetypes.name: Golden Handcuffs
archetypes.description: Extrinsic-dominant, Flickering. The Golden Handcuffs profile stays primarily for the rewards and compensation, but finds little intrinsic satisfaction in the work itself. They are reliable but not energised.
key_traits: Reliable performer — will meet expectations
Values alignment prevents active disengagement
Stable presence in the organisation

archetypes.name: Drifter
archetypes.description: No clear dominant, Flickering. The Drifter lacks a clear dominant motivation source. They are not strongly driven by intrinsic satisfaction, external rewards, purpose alignment, or growth.
key_traits: Often capable — the issue is motivation, not ability
May be in a transition period between motivational phases
Flexible — not locked into one motivational pattern

archetypes.name: Burned-Out
archetypes.description: Depleted, Fading. The Burned-Out profile shows structural depletion across intrinsic motivation, confidence, and growth orientation. Serious engagement state requiring immediate attention.
key_traits: Often were high performers before depletion set in
Recovery is possible with the right intervention
Typically have deep capability and institutional knowledge

archetypes.name: Frozen Asset
archetypes.description: Blocked, Fading. The Frozen Asset has strong values alignment but low confidence and low growth orientation have led to a state of structural paralysis. They are capable but stuck.
key_traits: Strong values alignment — genuinely committed to the organisation's mission
Often significant untapped capability beneath the paralysis
Loyal and stable — will not leave easily
